topic: Lambda Capture Scope Separation in Init Capture
explanation: When utilizing init capture in C++14 (`[ closure_member = initializer_expression ]`), the identifier on the left-hand side of the equals sign defines the name of the new data member within the generated closure class. The expression on the right-hand side is evaluated in the scope surrounding the lambda definition. This fundamental scope separation allows the right-hand side to reference existing local variables (e.g., `pw`) and the left-hand side to define the internal state name (e.g., `pw`) for the closure, enabling operations like moving the local variable into the closure member.
practical_example: A misunderstanding of the scope rules might lead a developer to believe that the RHS variable is immediately destroyed or shadowed by the LHS variable name, causing confusion when debugging complex initialization expressions or when trying to capture a variable under a different name.
keywords: Init capture, Generalized lambda capture, Lambda capture scope separation
chapter: Item 32: Use init capture to move objects into closures
book: Effective Modern C++ by Scott Meyers
